title: AIAS Certification Master Plan
purpose: Establish the official external maturity and certification architecture for AIAS without unsupported claims.
scope: CMMI-DEV V3.0 ML5, CMMI AIM, ISO 9001, ISO/IEC 27001, ISO/IEC 42001, ISO 22301, authorities, sequencing, version monitoring, evidence readiness and professional boundaries.

requirements.title: Official maturity objective
requirements.statement: The program shall designate CMMI-DEV V3.0 Maturity Level 5 as the sole primary organizational maturity objective.
requirements.rationale: Prevent ambiguous or competing Level 5 claims.
acceptance_criteria: Implementation exists or is formally planned.

requirements.title: AI maturity and management
requirements.statement: CMMI AIM shall be mandatory and ISO/IEC 42001 shall govern the certifiable AI management system.
requirements.rationale: Cover both AI maturity and responsible AI management.
acceptance_criteria: Implementation exists or is formally planned.

requirements.title: Integrated management system
requirements.statement: The plan shall target quality, information security, AI management and business continuity through ISO 9001, ISO/IEC 27001, ISO/IEC 42001 and ISO 22301.
acceptance_criteria: Implementation exists or is formally planned.

requirements.title: External authority boundary
requirements.statement: AIAS shall not self-issue CMMI ratings, ISO certificates or professional engineering approvals.
acceptance_criteria: Implementation exists or is formally planned.

requirements.title: Honest readiness
requirements.statement: Internal evidence assessment shall never claim external conformity, certification or appraisal rating.
acceptance_criteria: Implementation exists or is formally planned.

requirements.title: Version and copyright governance
requirements.statement: The plan shall monitor normative revisions and shall not reproduce unlicensed standards or model content.
requirements.rationale: Keep the program current and lawful.
acceptance_criteria: Implementation exists or is formally planned.

risks: Generated engineering output requires human review.
